title: Reuse exact canonical TensorAxis label tuples
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorAxis labels are already a bounded, validated, sorted and unique immutable tuple after construction, but TensorAxis.__post_init__ always routed even an exact already-canonical tuple through _sorted_strings. That path materializes a list, a duplicate-detection set, a sorted list and a new tuple before retaining the same label sequence. TypedAxis already demonstrates the intended canonical-container reuse pattern for the relation-block projection, so adding a cache or second axis representation would be redundant.
primary_claim: TensorAxis now recognizes an exact tuple whose labels are already valid, NUL-free, strictly sorted and unique and retains that tuple by object identity. Non-tuple or non-canonical input still falls back to the existing _sorted_strings canonicalizer, preserving deterministic ordering and duplicate refusal. Fourfold authority, TensorView sparse semantics, relation semantics, wire serialization and digest semantics are unchanged.
gardener_decision: Reuse the exact canonical immutable label container rather than add an axis cache, label index, adapter or second tensor representation. Keep the established _sorted_strings path only for inputs that actually need canonicalization. This reduces redundant canonical-path materialization while preserving one TensorAxis representation and the existing fail-closed boundary.
acceptance: an exact canonical TensorAxis labels tuple is retained by object identity after validation
oversized label sequences are still refused before element access
non-canonical bounded inputs still use deterministic sorting and duplicate refusal through the existing canonicalizer
NUL-containing and invalid labels remain fail closed
